record.paper_title: Analysis on Faddeev Knots and Skyrme Solitons: Recent Progress and Open Problems
record.original_question: Under the hedgehog ansatz in the three-dimensional Skyrme model, one obtains static critical points that minimize the energy within the radially symmetric class for each integer topological charge N. Are any of these hedgehog critical points absolute minimizers of the full Skyrme energy among all finite-energy fields of the same topological degree, rather than only within the radially symmetric subclass?

evidence.quote: that, for any integer N, (6.6) has a solution which may be obtained as the energy minimizer of (6.7) subject to the boundary condition stated in (6.6). See [26, 92]. In other words, among any topological class in π3(S3), the static Skyrme energy has a critical point which minimizes the energy functional among all radially symmetric field configurations. This result, although simple, is in sharp contrast with what we know for the sine–Gordon model where critical points of the energy of higher topological charges do not exist, as illustrated in Section 2. However, it is not known whether any of these critical points would be the absolute energy minimizers for the Skyrme model.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the static Skyrme energy on $\mathbb{R}^3$ for maps $U:\mathbb{R}^3 \to SU(2) \cong S^3$ satisfying $U(x) \to I$ as $|x|\to\infty$, given by
$$E(U) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\Big(\tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{tr}(\partial_i U^{-1}\partial_i U) \;+\; \tfrac{1}{16}\,\mathrm{tr}\big([\partial_i U^{-1}\,\partial_j U,\,\partial_j U^{-1}\,\partial_i U]\big)\Big)\,dx,$$
(written here up to a positive constant normalization of the Skyrme term). Each finite-energy configuration $U$ has a well-defined integer topological degree $N \in \pi_3(S^3) \cong \mathbb{Z}$. For each integer $N$, the hedgehog ansatz takes the form
$$U_N(x) = \cos f(r)\, I + i\, \sin f(r)\, \big(\hat{x}\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\big)^{(N)},$$
where $r=|x|$, $\hat{x}=x/r$, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}=(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$ are the Pauli matrices, the superscript $(N)$ denotes the standard degree-$N$ extension consistent with topological charge $N$, and $f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ is a profile function with $f(0)=N\pi$ and $f(\infty)=0$. It is known that for every integer $N$ there exists a profile $f$ minimizing the Skyrme energy within the radially symmetric (hedgehog) class of degree $N$, yielding a static critical point $U_N$ of $E$.

Question: For some (or any) integer $N$, is the hedgehog critical point $U_N$ an absolute minimizer of $E$ among all finite-energy configurations $U:\mathbb{R}^3 \to SU(2)$ of topological degree $N$ (not merely among radially symmetric ones)?
artifact.status_search_result: For topological degrees $|N|\geq 2$, numerical and analytical studies (e.g., toroidal, Platonic-symmetric Skyrmions) indicate that the energy minimizers are not radially symmetric, so the hedgehog is not the absolute minimizer in those sectors. For $N=\pm 1$, the hedgehog is widely believed to be the absolute minimizer, but a rigorous mathematical proof in the full unconstrained class does not appear to be established. Thus the question is partially resolved: a clear "no" for higher $|N|$, while the $|N|=1$ case remains open in the rigorous sense.

status_evidence.title: Skyrmion - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The hedgehog Skyrmion is almost certainly the minimal energy static solution in the B=1 sector...
status_evidence.claim: For B=1 the hedgehog is believed but not rigorously proven to be the absolute minimizer.

status_evidence.title: Hedgehog and toroidal solitons of the Skyrme model
status_evidence.snippet: Toroidal solitons of the Skyrme model with lower energy than hedgehog configurations of the same topological charge.
status_evidence.claim: For higher topological charges, non-hedgehog (e.g., toroidal) configurations have lower Skyrme energy, so hedgehogs are not absolute minimizers there.

status_evidence.title: A Smörgåsbord of Skyrmions
status_evidence.snippet: Higher-charge Skyrmion minimizers exhibit Platonic and other non-spherical symmetries.
status_evidence.claim: Energy minimizers in higher charge sectors are not radially symmetric.
